# Psalm 31 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Translator:** SOPHIA (Council Arbiter) | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** For the choirmaster. A psalm of David.

**2** In You, O LORD, I take refuge; let me never be put to shame; in Your righteousness deliver me!

**3** Incline Your ear to me; rescue me speedily! Be a rock of refuge for me, a strong fortress to save me!

**4** For You are my rock and my fortress; and for Your name's sake You lead me and guide me;

**5** You take me out of the net they have hidden for me, for You are my refuge.

**6** Into Your hand I commit my spirit; You have redeemed me, O LORD, faithful God.

**7** I hate those who pay regard to worthless idols, but I trust in the LORD.

**8** I will rejoice and be glad in Your steadfast love, because You have seen my affliction; You have known the distress of my soul,

**9** and You have not delivered me into the hand of the enemy; You have set my feet in a broad place.

**10** Be gracious to me, O LORD, for I am in distress; my eye is wasted from grief; my soul and my body also.

**11** For my life is spent with sorrow, and my years with sighing; my strength fails because of my iniquity, and my bones waste away.

**12** Because of all my adversaries I have become a reproach, especially to my neighbors, and an object of dread to my acquaintances; those who see me in the street flee from me.

**13** I have been forgotten like one who is dead; I have become like a broken vessel.

**14** For I hear the whispering of many — terror on every side! — as they scheme together against me, as they plot to take my life.

**15** But I trust in You, O LORD; I say, 'You are my God.'

**16** My times are in Your hand; rescue me from the hand of my enemies and from my persecutors!

**17** Make Your face shine on Your servant; save me in Your steadfast love!

**18** O LORD, let me not be put to shame, for I call upon You; let the wicked be put to shame; let them go silently to Sheol.

**19** Let the lying lips be mute, which speak insolently against the righteous in pride and contempt.

**20** Oh, how abundant is Your goodness, which You have stored up for those who fear You and worked for those who take refuge in You, in the sight of the children of mankind!

**21** In the shelter of Your presence You hide them from the plots of men; You store them in Your shelter from the strife of tongues.

**22** Blessed be the LORD, for He has wondrously shown His steadfast love to me when I was in a besieged city.

**23** I had said in my alarm, 'I am cut off from Your sight.' But You heard the voice of my pleas for mercy when I cried to You for help.

**24** Love the LORD, all you His saints! The LORD preserves the faithful but abundantly repays the one who acts in pride.

---
## Council Notes

SOPHIA detected **6** significant divergence(s) in Psalm 31.

- **31:1** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **31:2** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **31:8** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **31:9** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **31:11** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **31:13** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

## Translation Notes (Select)

### EMET
- **31:6**: Into Your hand I commit my spirit — Jesus quotes this verse from the cross (Luke 23:46). The psalm becomes the final prayer of the Crucified.
- **31:14**: 'Terror on every side' (magor missaviv) — Jeremiah's signature phrase (Jer 20:3, 10). The psalm shares vocabulary with the prophetic tradition.

### LOGOS
- **31:16**: 'My times are in Your hand' — a comprehensive surrender. Not just this moment but all moments — past, present, future — belong to God.

### PNEUMA
- **31:6**: Jesus' last words from the cross come from this verse. Stephen also prayed it while being stoned (Acts 7:59). The psalm became the prayer for those dying in faith.

— SOPHIA
